messages.subject: lavaan ERROR when fitting SEM
parts:
model <- '
# Latent variables
Socio =~ sex + age + education + marital + incomemonth

# regression
Hypertension ~ Socio + bmi + waistcirc + smokecurr 
'
fit <- sem(model, data = Filtered, estimator = "MLR")

Error in lav_samplestats_icov(COV = cov[[g]], ridge = ridge, x.idx = x.idx[[g]],  : 
  lavaan ERROR: sample covariance matrix is not positive-definite

Above it's my R code, however, am getting an error message when running it. Any help or suggestion??


Hypertension its dummy code 0 or 1.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: lavaan ERROR when fitting SEM
parts:
# Latent variables
Socio =~ sex + age + education + marital + incomemonth

Socio is a formative construct, not reflective.  I'm guessing those variables are not remotely related enough to even trick the software into thinking there is a single common source of variance, but I'm not sure why the matrix would be NPD unless there is multicollinearity among the variables.  Before you persist in thinking this model should even be fitted to data, read this article:

Rhemtulla, M., van Bork, R., & Borsboom, D. (2018). Worse than measurement error: Consequences of inappropriate latent variable measurement models. Preprint available from https://osf.io/f8g4d/

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.subject: Re: lavaan ERROR when fitting SEM
parts:
Peter--
     The "formative" operator <~ is know to be wonky. I recommend you not use it. But that will not induce the observed variable covariance matrix to be not positive definite. That is strictly an attribute of the data. 
     I am not a fan of VIF and related. I encourage you to look at the correlation matrix itself. There are not so many variables to consider. I also suggest, since you have a key variable that is dichotomous, to look at the correlation matrix separately for the 0 and 1 cases. If you have missing data, the missing data handling prcedure may also induce the covariance matrix to become not positive definite.

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: lavaan ERROR when fitting SEM
parts:
Peter,
The roll that various variables play in your SE model does not have any impact on how you go about investigating a NPD input matrix.  You need to consider all the variables that are used by the SE model because they are all included in the matrix referred to in the warning.

To do this using the vif() function from the car package, I think that you would need to create a dummy IV for the lm() fit.  However, I generally prefer the original R^2 scale (0,1) to the transformed VIF scale (1, +Inf), in part because the most interesting value on the R^2 scale is not defined on the VIF scale.  So, I use the itemanal() function in the rela package.  The only trick is that it wants a matrix rather that a data frame as input.

round(cor(myData),2)
myOutput <- itemanal(as.matrix(myData)) # If there are any unused variables in the data set, filter them out with indices
myOutput$Alpha.Stats$Squared.multiple.cor  # Ignore the rest of the output because you are not doing item analysis

I agree with Ed that it is important not to ignore the correlation matrix.  However, it is also possible for a set of variables with relatively low bivariate correlations to produce colinearlity.  So, I like to look at the R-square for each variable too.  You can also supplement the above analyses with these:

det(cor(myData))
eigen(cor(myData))  

Of course, you can also substitute cov() where I have used cor().  I like to roll all of the above into one function and arrange all the output in a single list.

Keith
------------------------
Keith A. Markus
John Jay College of Criminal Justice, CUNY
http://jjcweb.jjay.cuny.edu/kmarkus
Frontiers of Test Validity Theory: Measurement, Causation and Meaning.
http://www.routledge.com/books/details/9781841692203/
